title: General Tso's Chicken
summary: Crisply fried chicken thigh pieces are tossed in a sweet-sour, lightly spiced sauce with garlic, ginger and dried chillies, served with broccoli and rice.
equipment: heavy pot or deep casserole (at least 24 cm, 5 litres)
steamer or saucepan for the broccoli

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3 cm pieces
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Toss the chicken with the egg white and soy sauce and leave for 15-30 minutes, which seasons the meat and helps the coating stick.

steps.title: Make the craggy coating
steps.text: Whisk together the cornflour, flour and baking powder, then add 2 tbsp of the marinade liquid and rub it through with your fingers to form small clumps - this gives the coating a rougher, crunchier texture than a smooth batter. Dredge the chicken in it, pressing the coating on, then set the pieces on the rack.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Heat 4-5cm of oil in a heavy pot to 175°C. Fry the chicken in 3 batches for 4-5 minutes each until golden, crisp and the centre reaches 74°C, draining on the rack and letting the oil return to 175°C between batches.

steps.title: Steam the broccoli
steps.text: Steam the broccoli florets for 3-4 minutes until bright green and just tender.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Stir together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, stock and cornflour with the sesame oil.

steps.title: Stir-fry the aromatics and sauce
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high, add the dried chillies for 15 seconds, then the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites for 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce mixture and stir until it boils and turns thick and glossy, about 1 minute; the balance of flavour comes from the soy, vinegar and sugar.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Take the wok off the heat, add the fried chicken, and toss quickly to coat - tossing it in off the heat keeps the coating crisp rather than softening it in the hot sauce. Scatter with the spring onion greens and sesame seeds, and serve with the broccoli and rice.

tips: Let the oil return to 175°C between frying batches, or the chicken will turn greasy rather than crisp.
Common mistake: leaving the fried chicken sitting in the hot sauce for too long. Toss it through quickly off the heat so the crust stays crunchy.
Rubbing a little marinade liquid into the dry coating before dredging is what gives the craggy, extra-crunchy texture.
Steam the broccoli just until bright green - overcooking turns it dull and soft.
Have everything prepped before you start the final stir-fry, as the sauce thickens and the chicken needs tossing in within a minute or two.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten fresh, as the coating softens on standing. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat in a hot oven or air fryer until piping hot (74°C) to help recrisp the coating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
